senses.gloss:
Vehat seems to mean a ‘cow that miscarries.’ It is mentioned in the Atharvaveda and later.
Foot notes xii. 4, 37 et seq. In iii. 23, 1, a woman is called vehat.
Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, xviii. 27; xxiv. 1, etc.; taittirīya Saṃhitā, ii. 1, 5, 3, etc. In Śatapatha brāhmaṇa, xii. 4, 4, 6, Eggeling, Sacred Books of the East, 44, 195, adopts the sense ‘a cow desiring the bull.’ But cf. Whitney, Translation of the Atharvaveda, 127.
Vehat occurs in conjunction with vaśā in the kāṭhaka Saṃhitā (xxxviii. 10), the Maitrāyaṇī Saṃhitā (iii. 11, 11), the Vājasaneyī Saṃhitā (xxi. 21), and the taittirīya brāhmaṇa (ii. 6, 18, 4).
